messages:
sam: Heads-up: hitting steady RSS growth on long-context inference workers — looks like KV pinball / fragmentation rather than leaks. :thinking_face:
maria: Which job / model? any reproducer?
sam: rtx-p3 pool, gptx-16k workload (many long prompts). Repro in perf-ci with synthetic longctx stream. Here's the mem trace snippet from the profiler run this morning:

sam: ```
2026-03-17T09:12:01Z worker-12 INFO kv_alloc: total_alloc=2.3G free=320M free_frag=1.6G allocations=124k
2026-03-17T09:15:01Z worker-12 INFO kv_alloc: total_alloc=2.9G free=200M free_frag=2.1G allocations=149k
2026-03-17T09:18:01Z worker-12 INFO kv_cache: pages_in_use=3.1K pages_free=140 pages_frag_pct=67.2
```

tanner: Oof. That free_frag number + high frag_pct screams many small leftover slots. Any pattern in allocation sizes?
sam: Yes — heatmap from profiler: heavy churn around 512B, 1KB, and a tail at 4KB. Large KV slices (32KB+) are OK. Small-block junk accumulates and isn't being coalesced.
rachel: Could be our allocator bin thresholds. We're currently using power-of-two buckets up to 8KB, then slab for 16KB+. If long sequences create many partial KV entries, they fragment the mid bins.
maria: Related: paging/eviction seems to prefer LRU-ish page evict but it evicts whole pages (64KB). When small slots are scattered across pages we end up with mostly-empty pages and evict hot items or keep cold dense pages. Pinball effect.
sam: Exactly. I see repeated re-materialization of KV spans even though total "used" tokens are similar. Batching suffers: avg token latency up ~8% and throughput down ~12% during the drift window.
tanner: Any quick mitigation? Increase page compaction frequency or coalesce small frees?
rachel: Two immediate ideas: (1) aggressive background compactor that merges same-page free runs into larger arenas, (2) change allocator to favor same-size re-use (per-thread free lists pinned by size class) + deferred reclaim to reduce scattering.

sam: I sketched a compactor proto. Config knobs: compact_threshold_pct (current 70), compaction_interval_s (current 600), page_scan_limit (current 100 pages/interval). Proposal: reduce threshold to 50, interval to 60s, page_scan_limit to 500, and stop compacting pages with >90% recent reads to avoid thrashing.

sam: ```json
{"kv_compaction": {"compact_threshold_pct": 50, "compaction_interval_s": 60, "page_scan_limit": 500, "protect_hot_pct": 90}}
```

maria: That seems fine but risk is CPU impact of scanning. What did perf-ci show if we simulate interval=60?
sam: Perf-ci run: compactor at 60s increased background CPU by ~4% on p3. But RSS returned to baseline in ~10min and throughput recovered. No visible latency spikes on tail.
tanner: Good. Still smells like allocator policy is root cause. We should avoid pure power-of-two bins for small churning sizes; consider mixed-size bucket (e.g., 256/384/512/768/1k) to reduce internal fragmentation.
rachel: Agree. Also consider per-page freelist that prefers reusing slots on same page if possible (page-local reuse) — reduces scattering and makes page-level eviction decisions meaningful.

ci-bot: [deploy-preview] compactor-config (sam) queued for perf-ci 1719012000.

maria: For long-term, propose an A/B in canary: change allocator to page-local freelist + mid-size non-power-of-two classes, and run for 24h against synthetic longctx traces. If improvement >5% throughput or frag_pct drop >15 points, roll. Otherwise revert.
sam: I'll draft the RFC + perf harness. Quick checklist:
- add metrics: per-size free_count, page_density (used_bytes/page_bytes), page_reuse_hits
- add trace labels in tracer when compactor touches a page
- tune compactor rate limiting and hot-protect heuristic

tanner: Also add a small experiment: pre-warm pools with typical small sizes from observed heatmap to reduce first-time fragmentation on startup.
maria: One more: kernel selection/batching note — if KV latency goes up due to background compaction it can interfere with our continuous-batching SLO window. Add a temporary pause-compactor-during-large-batch flag (defaults on).
sam: Nice. I'll include that in the RFC. Who wants to review the perf-ci results when they land?
rachel: Me + maria. I'll also run a memory-alloc microbench to validate coalescing improvement.
sam: Thanks — filing the perf job and RFC. Will drop links here when available. :thumbsup:
